theory.intro: To multiply by a 2-digit number, split **both** numbers by place value and use the area model, or use the standard algorithm.
facts: The algorithm multiplies by the ones, then the tens (shifted one place), then adds.
steps: Split each number into tens and ones.
Multiply every part of one by every part of the other.
Add all the part-products for the total.

workedExamples.question_text: Use the standard algorithm to calculate $58\times24$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Multiply by the ones, then by the tens.
$58\times4=232$.
The $2$ in $24$ represents $20$, so $58\times20=1160$.
$\begin{array}{r}58\\\times24\\\hline232\\1160\\\hline1392\end{array}$
So $58\times24=1392$.

workedExamples.question_text:
For $207\times36$:
(a) calculate the product using the standard algorithm
(b) explain why the second partial product ends in zero.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) $207\times6=1242$.
$207\times30=6210$.
$\begin{array}{r}207\\\times36\\\hline1242\\6210\\\hline7452\end{array}$
So $207\times36=7452$.
(b) The $3$ represents $30$. Multiplying $207$ by $3$ gives $621$; multiplying by $30$ gives $6210$. The zero keeps the tens partial product in its correct place.

workedExamples.question_text:
A student calculates $37\times26$ using the partial products $222$ and $74$.
Identify the error and give the correct product.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$37\times6=222$ is correct.
The $2$ in $26$ represents $20$, not $2$.
The second partial product should be $37\times20=740$.
$222+740=962$.
So $37\times26=962$.

workedExamples.question_text: Find the missing digit in $4\square3\times12=5676$. Check using partial products.
workedExamples.solution_text:
The missing digit is $7$.
Check $473\times12$ by multiplying by $2$ and by $10$.
$473\times2=946$.
$473\times10=4730$.
$946+4730=5676$.
So $473\times12=5676$, as required.

In the algorithm for $413 \times 22$, explain why the second partial product is $8260$, not $826$.
Then find the product.
development.solution_text:
The second digit represents $2$ tens, so $413 \times 20=8260$.
$413 \times 2=826$.
$826+8260$
$=9086$

mastery.question_text:
An area model for $76 \times 63$ has part-products $4200$, $210$, $360$ and $18$.
Explain which multiplication produces each part, then find the total.

A student uses the algorithm for $43 \times 26$ and writes partial products $258$ and $86$.
Identify the error and find the product.
Complete the multiplication $3\square 2 \times 14=4508$ by finding the missing digit.
mastery.solution_text:
The missing digit is $2$.
Check $322\times14$ using the ones and tens partial products.
$322\times4=1288$.
$322\times10=3220$.
$1288+3220=4508$.
So $322\times14=4508$, as required.
